code-expression-lookalike-literals.title: Literals that look like code references but are not

compose-default-value-holds-literal-cred.title: A Compose default or alternative value that is itself a credential literal

Paired with the same line whose default is empty (${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}) and the required form (${GITHUB_TOKEN:?message}), which hold no credential bytes.

compose-resolved-config-renders-referenc.title: Docker Compose rendered configuration holds the value its source only referenced
compose-resolved-config-renders-referenc.summary: A Compose file whose environment entry for GITHUB_TOKEN only names a variable (GITHUB_TOKEN: ${GITHUB_TOKEN}), and the canonical configuration that docker compose config prints from it, where the same key holds the resolved credential-shaped literal. The rendered text is a different artifact from the source, with the same keys.

connection-key-value-quoted-and-delimite.title: Passwords in key-value connection strings: quoted, escaped and delimiter-terminated
connection-key-value-quoted-and-delimite.summary: Key-value connection strings that hold a synthetic password: libpq keyword/value with single quotes, a space and backslash escapes; an ADO.NET string where the password ends at a semicolon; the MySQL key-value form with a quoted string; and a Kafka SASL/PLAIN JAAS line with a double-quoted password ending at a semicolon.

connection-passwords-empty-or-omitted.title: Connection strings with an empty or omitted password
connection-passwords-empty-or-omitted.summary: Connection strings with the password slot present but empty (user followed by a colon and then the at-sign, password:'', Password=;) or omitted entirely (user only, keyword absent), across MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis and OLE DB forms.

connection-passwords-supplied-by-referen.title: Connection passwords supplied by interpolation, environment or password file
connection-passwords-supplied-by-referen.summary: Connection strings whose password position holds an interpolation expression (${DB_PASSWORD}, ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?...}), whose password is read from a file named by passfile, or which rely on the REDISCLI_AUTH environment variable instead of a literal in the command line.

connection-public-metadata-without-passw.title: Public host, database, vhost and user parts of connection strings
connection-public-metadata-without-passw.summary: Connection strings and key-value strings that carry only public parts: host, port, database, replica or cluster name, AMQP vhost (including %2F), user name, and Windows integrated authentication, with no password slot.

connection-uri-percent-encoded-password-.title: Percent-encoded passwords in connection URIs: the span is the encoded text as written
connection-uri-percent-encoded-password-.summary: Connection URIs for MongoDB, MySQL and an AMQP broker whose password contains reserved characters written as percent-encoded triplets (%40, %3A, %2F, %23, %25, %5B, %5D) in the user-info position. Synthetic passwords on reserved example hosts.

connection-uri-placeholder-lookalike-pas.title: Passwords that only resemble a placeholder
connection-uri-placeholder-lookalike-pas.summary: Connection URIs whose password imitates a placeholder but carries real-looking material: filler characters ending in a real-looking character, a placeholder word embedded in a long random value, or a placeholder word prefixed to one.

connection-uri-placeholder-passwords.title: Placeholder passwords in connection URI templates
connection-uri-placeholder-passwords.summary: Connection URIs whose password is an instruction to the reader, such as your_password_here, insert-password-here or REPLACE_ME_PASSWORD.

connection-uri-unencoded-sub-delimiter-p.title: Passwords holding unencoded sub-delimiters in connection URIs
connection-uri-unencoded-sub-delimiter-p.summary: Connection URIs (AMQP, Redis) whose password contains RFC 3986 sub-delimiters (! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =) written without percent-encoding. Synthetic passwords.

content-digest-references-in-build-and-p.title: Content digests in image references, integrity attributes and package metadata
content-digest-references-in-build-and-p.summary: Several kinds of content digest in developer artifacts: an OCI image reference pinned by sha256 digest, an HTML script tag with a Subresource Integrity attribute, an npm lock-file integrity field, Go go.sum h1 hashes and pip requirement hashes. Alphabets are lowercase hex (64 characters) and standard Base64 (44 to 88 characters), each behind an algorithm tag.

contentful-oauth-access-token-redirect-f.title: Contentful OAuth access token in a redirect URI hash fragment
contentful-oauth-access-token-redirect-f.summary: A synthetic OAuth access token as the access_token parameter in the hash fragment of a redirect URI, in a bare URL, in a Location response header and in a quoted JSON string.

contentful-oauth-client-id-and-token-pla.title: Contentful OAuth client ids, scopes, placeholders and masked displays
contentful-oauth-client-id-and-token-pla.summary: An authorization request with a client id and scope, the documented fragment placeholder, and a reference, a masked display and prose under the access_token name.

credential-bytes-divided-between-stream-.title: Intact credential bytes divided between stream chunks
credential-bytes-divided-between-stream-.summary: The bytes of one intact SendGrid-shaped key are divided between chunks of a stream or string at a chosen boundary; no byte of the key is changed.

credential-in-base64-text-part-wrapped-a.title: Credential value in a MIME base64 text part wrapped across encoded lines
credential-in-base64-text-part-wrapped-a.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key is the whole body of a MIME text part whose Content-Transfer-Encoding is base64: the key's 69 octets encode to 92 characters, written as a 76-character line and a 16-character line with a CRLF between them. The key is recoverable only by ignoring the line break and Base64-decoding the two fragments together.

credential-in-opentelemetry-log-record-f.title: The same credential in different OpenTelemetry log record fields
credential-in-opentelemetry-log-record-f.summary: One synthetic GitHub classic personal access token literal is placed, in turn, in the string body of an OTLP/JSON log record, in a map-and-array nested body, in an attribute value, in exception text (message and stack trace), in a resource attribute and inside a body string that holds serialized JSON, while the same record always carries a trace id and a span id. A last record holds two distinct literals and a trace id in upper-case hex.

credential-key-ending-a-line.title: A credential-sounding key at the end of a line
credential-key-ending-a-line.summary: A YAML block key such as secret: followed by nested keys on the next lines, and password prompts such as Password: or an SSH prompt that end a line, each followed by unrelated text on the next line.

credential-key-with-same-line-value.title: A credential-sounding key with its value on the same line
credential-key-with-same-line-value.summary: password: followed by a synthetic literal on the same line, once with a space and once with a horizontal tab and a CRLF line ending.

credential-prefix-before-unrelated-line.title: Credential prefix at a line end before unrelated text
credential-prefix-before-unrelated-line.summary: A line ends with the SendGrid key prefix, or with the prefix and a short unrelated token, and the next line holds ordinary prose or an unrelated public encoded string.

credential-split-across-concatenated-str.title: Credential split across adjacent or added string literals
credential-split-across-concatenated-str.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key is written as two string pieces that the language joins: adjacent literals in Python, or two literals added with the plus operator in JavaScript and Python.

credential-split-by-backslash-crlf-conti.title: Credential split by a backslash followed by CRLF
credential-split-by-backslash-crlf-conti.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in an unquoted shell assignment is broken by a backslash followed by a carriage return and a line feed, as a script saved with Windows line endings would hold.

credential-split-by-backslash-newline-in.title: Credential split by a backslash-newline inside single quotes
credential-split-by-backslash-newline-in.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in a shell single-quoted value is broken by a backslash and line feed, so the backslash and the line feed stay inside the value.

credential-split-by-literal-line-break-i.title: Credential split by a literal LF or CRLF in plain text
credential-split-by-literal-line-break-i.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in plain text (a note, an email body, a log) is broken by a literal line feed or a carriage return plus line feed, with no construct that joins the lines.

credential-split-by-markdown-paragraph-l.title: Credential wrapped by a Markdown paragraph or code-span line ending
credential-split-by-markdown-paragraph-l.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in a Markdown paragraph, or inside an inline code span, is wrapped across a line ending.

credential-split-by-quoted-printable-sof.title: Credential split across lines by a quoted-printable soft line break in a MIME text part
credential-split-by-quoted-printable-sof.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key is assigned on one line of a MIME text part whose Content-Transfer-Encoding is quoted-printable. The encoded line is cut at 76 characters by a soft line break (an equal sign ending the line), so the key is written as two fragments with an equal sign and a CRLF between them, and the assignment's own equal sign is written =3D. The key is intact only after quoted-printable decoding.

credential-split-by-shell-backslash-newl.title: Credential split across lines by an unquoted shell line continuation
credential-split-by-shell-backslash-newl.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key assigned in a shell script is broken after some character by an unquoted (or double-quoted) backslash and line feed, so the value continues on the next line.

credential-split-by-string-literal-line-.title: Credential split across lines by a string-literal line continuation
credential-split-by-string-literal-line-.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key inside a Python or JavaScript string literal is broken by a backslash at a line end, so the literal continues on the next line.

credential-with-escaped-line-break-text.title: Credential value containing escaped line-break text
credential-with-escaped-line-break-text.summary: A SendGrid-shaped key inside a JSON string, or in a log line, holds an escaped line break (a backslash and the letter n) between two fragments.

docker-config-auth-field-base64-username.title: Docker config.json: base64 auth value for a registry
docker-config-auth-field-base64-username.summary: A synthetic Docker config.json whose auths map holds a base64 auth string per registry (one registry, then two registries).

docker-config-credential-store-and-helpe.title: Docker config.json: credential store and helper references
docker-config-credential-store-and-helpe.summary: Synthetic Docker config.json files that configure credsStore, or a credHelpers map of registry domains to helper names, and hold no auth value.

documented-public-key-value-under-matchi.title: Documented public key value under a matching or ordinary field label

workflow-command-literal-credential-in-c.title: Literal installation token in a workflow command line
workflow-command-literal-credential-in-c.summary: A synthetic ghs_ installation token written as a literal in the text of a workflow step: inside an echo of NAME=value to the GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT environment file, and as the argument of an add-mask workflow command.

workflow-command-reference-and-masked-va.title: Expression, variable reference or runner mask where a workflow command would carry a token
workflow-command-reference-and-masked-va.summary: Workflow command lines and log text where the credential position holds an expression (${{ secrets.NAME }}), a shell variable reference ($NAME) as the add-mask argument or an environment-file value, a secret that expands to an empty string, or the runner's *** mask.

x-bearer-token-authorization-header-valu.title: X bearer token in an Authorization header
x-bearer-token-authorization-header-valu.summary: A synthetic token after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header of an X API request, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map. The values contain only letters, digits and hyphens.

x-oauth1-access-token-secret-field.title: X OAuth 1.0a access token secret in an oauth_token_secret field
x-oauth1-access-token-secret-field.summary: A synthetic access token secret after oauth_token_secret in a form-encoded body next to oauth_token, in a JSON object and in a shell assignment.

x-oauth1-token-identity-and-signature-no.title: X OAuth 1.0a token identity, signature, placeholders and masked displays
x-oauth1-token-identity-and-signature-no.summary: An OAuth Authorization header that holds oauth_token and oauth_signature, an oauth_token_secret property that holds a placeholder, a reference or a masked display, and prose that names the field.

x-oauth2-client-secret-basic-envelope.title: X OAuth 2.0 client secret in a Basic envelope
x-oauth2-client-secret-basic-envelope.summary: A synthetic encoded credential after the Basic scheme in the Authorization header of a token request, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map. The encoded value is the base64 of a synthetic client id and a synthetic client secret joined by a colon.

x-oauth2-ids-and-bearer-placeholders-non.title: X OAuth 2.0 client ids, user ids, placeholders and masked displays
x-oauth2-ids-and-bearer-placeholders-non.summary: A public client id in an authorization request, a user id in a response, Bearer and Basic placeholders, environment and template references, masked displays and a scheme with no value.

x-oauth2-refresh-token-form-field-and-re.title: Value of refresh_token in an X OAuth 2.0 token exchange
x-oauth2-refresh-token-form-field-and-re.summary: A synthetic value of the refresh_token form field in a refresh request, shown as a curl --data-urlencode argument and a raw HTTP form body behind a Basic header placeholder, and of the refresh_token member in a token response excerpt.

x-oauth2-refresh-token-placeholders-and-.title: X OAuth 2.0 refresh_token placeholders and non-value fields
x-oauth2-refresh-token-placeholders-and-.summary: A refresh_token field holding an angle placeholder, a template or shell reference, a masked or empty value, a prose mention, and a token response with only the type, lifetime and scope members.

yaml-flow-collection-secret-keys.title: secret as a structural key in YAML flow collections
yaml-flow-collection-secret-keys.summary: Flow-style YAML such as volumes: [{name: tls, secret: {secretName: web-tls-cert}}] and secret: [configReference, anotherReference], where secret names a structure or lists references, including one with CRLF line endings.

zendesk-api-token-basic-credential-token.title: Token part of a documented {email_address}/token:{api_token} Basic credential string
zendesk-api-token-basic-credential-token.summary: A synthetic token after the /token: separator of an email-address username in a curl -u argument, a JSON configuration string and an environment assignment, for a Zendesk subdomain.

zendesk-api-token-lookalikes-and-non-val.title: Zendesk Basic credential strings with the email address, a template, a reference or a masked display in place of the token
zendesk-api-token-lookalikes-and-non-val.summary: An email address and subdomain with no token, the documented {email_address}/token:{api_token} template, a credential string whose token is an environment reference, a masked display, and an email-address username with the separator and no token.

zendesk-oauth-access-token-bearer-header.title: Value of an Authorization: Bearer header carrying a Zendesk OAuth access token
zendesk-oauth-access-token-bearer-header.summary: A synthetic value after Authorization: Bearer in a raw request to a subdomain host, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map.

zendesk-oauth-client-secret-token-reques.title: Value of a client_secret field in a Zendesk OAuth token request
zendesk-oauth-client-secret-token-reques.summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id in a raw form-encoded token request, a JSON body and a curl -d argument.

zendesk-oauth-lookalikes-and-non-values.title: Zendesk client identifiers, subdomains and placeholder Bearer or client_secret values
zendesk-oauth-lookalikes-and-non-values.summary: A client identifier and subdomain, the documented Authorization: Bearer {access_token} template, a scheme-only header, and Bearer or client_secret values that are placeholders, environment references or masked displays.

zendesk-oauth-refresh-token-json-member.title: Value of refresh_token in a Zendesk OAuth token request or response
zendesk-oauth-refresh-token-json-member.summary: A synthetic value of the refresh_token member in a JSON refresh request body, shown as a curl -d argument and a pretty-printed body, and of the refresh_token member in a token response excerpt.

zendesk-oauth-refresh-token-placeholders.title: Zendesk refresh_token placeholders and non-value members
zendesk-oauth-refresh-token-placeholders.summary: A refresh_token member holding an angle placeholder, the documented template, a template reference, a masked or empty value or a shell variable reference, a prose mention, and a response with only the type, scope and lifetime members.

zoom-build-api-key-placeholders-and-non-.title: Zoom Build platform API key placeholder, reference and masked display
zoom-build-api-key-placeholders-and-non-.summary: An x-api-key header that holds the documented placeholder, an environment reference, a masked display or nothing, a documented Bearer template, and prose that names the header.

zoom-build-api-key-x-api-key-header-valu.title: Zoom Build platform API key in an x-api-key header
zoom-build-api-key-x-api-key-header-valu.summary: A synthetic Build platform API key after an x-api-key header in a raw request, a curl option and a JSON header map.

zoom-client-secret-basic-envelope-and-fo.title: Zoom client secret in a token request Basic envelope or client_secret field
zoom-client-secret-basic-envelope-and-fo.summary: The encoded Basic credential of a synthetic client id and client secret in the Authorization header of an OAuth or Server-to-Server token request, shown as a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map, and a synthetic client_secret form field beside client_id.

zoom-client-secret-placeholders-and-publ.title: Zoom Basic header and client_secret placeholders and public ids
zoom-client-secret-placeholders-and-publ.summary: A scheme-only Basic header, placeholders, references, masked values, a client_secret field holding a placeholder or mask, a prose mention, and token requests that carry only the account id and client id.

zoom-oauth-refresh-token-response-member.title: Value of the refresh_token member in a Zoom token response
zoom-oauth-refresh-token-response-member.summary: A synthetic value of the refresh_token member in a Zoom user-authorization token response, shown as a pretty-printed JSON body, a compact JSON body behind raw HTTP response headers and the output of a curl request.

zoom-server-to-server-access-token-beare.title: Value of a Zoom Server-to-Server access token in a Bearer header or token response
zoom-server-to-server-access-token-beare.summary: A synthetic value of the access_token member in a token response for the account_credentials grant, and after Authorization: Bearer in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument.

zoom-token-lookalikes-and-non-values.title: Zoom account and client ids, documentation placeholders and masked token values
zoom-token-lookalikes-and-non-values.summary: An account id and client id in a token request, the grant type and expiry, and an access_token, Bearer or refresh_token value that is the documentation placeholder, an environment reference or a masked display.

zoom-webhook-signature-and-challenge-der.title: Zoom webhook signature, timestamp and challenge outputs next to the secret token's name
zoom-webhook-signature-and-challenge-der.summary: A webhook request whose headers hold x-zm-request-timestamp and an x-zm-signature value, a validation response with the plain challenge and its encrypted form, the documented signature placeholder, the signed message string, and references and prose that name the secret token.
